description:
## Goal

Make macro execution consume the persistent root product graph directly, then delete the synthetic scheduler bridge for backend programs.

## Current boundary

`BuildMacroExecutable` currently synthesizes `BuildBackendProduct`, waits on `FactKey::BackendProgram`, and deep-clones the World-owned program. That bridge is live today. Once root products persist, retaining a second fact/map authority requires an explicit movement protocol and risks stale post-edit programs.

## Strategy and proof

1. Give hidden macro roots the same persistent product ownership and exact invalidation contract as user roots.
2. Make macro executable production read the program-equality projection of `RootBackendProduct(root)` and react to its generation.
3. Prove unchanged macro calls reuse the settled program; reachable macro-source changes invalidate the exact reader closure; unrelated source and transport-only/program-equal movement do not relower it.
4. Delete `Job::BuildBackendProduct`, `FactKey::BackendProgram`, `BackendProgramMap`, product-to-fact copying, synthetic completion identity, and bridge-only tests/docs.
5. Preserve macro recursion/cycle behavior, exact causal attribution, canonical artifacts, and runtime behavior.
6. Run macro, library, fixture, determinism, formatting, and strict clippy checks.

No compatibility fact mirror remains after cutover.
title: Delete the BackendProgram scheduler bridge after macro roots join persistent products
